sources.citation: Ratliff, Martha. 2010. Hmong-Mien Language History. Pacific Linguistics 613. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p.11: 'Zongdi Hmong has twelve tonal contrasts including both level and contour tones (Wang and Mao 1995)'; p.199 family-level only: nominal prefixes 'are unstressed'. No Mashan-specific word-stress statement.

sources.citation: Wu Zhengbiao 吴正彪 & Yang Guangying 杨光应. 2010. 麻山次方言区苗文方案的设计与使用—兼谈苗族英雄史诗《亚鲁王》的记译整理问题. 民族翻译 2010(3): 58-65. (the Internet Archive)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Orthography for Central Mashan (Zongdi township, Dadiba village): initials, finals, 11 tone values by category (p.62); no 重音/轻声 statement.

sources.citation: Purnell, Herbert C. (ed.) 1972. Miao and Yao Linguistic Studies (Cornell SEAP Data Paper 88), incl. Miao Language Team 1962 'A brief description of the Miao language'
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ma shan subdialect survey point Chiao yi (Ziyun); Tsung ti (Zongdi) tone values in loanword tables; the word 'stress' does not occur.

sources.citation: Mortensen, David R. 2013. Tonally conditioned vowel raising in Shuijingping Mang. Journal of East Asian Linguistics 22(3): 189-216. doi:10.1007/s10831-013-9102-6 (author postprint from cs.cmu.edu/~dmortens)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: online with a university library login
sources.note: No word-stress statement. Describes Shuijingping (Zongdi township) tone system (A1 A1' A2 B1 B1' B2 C1 C1' C2 D1 D1' D2), left-to-right tone sandhi after A-tones and tonally conditioned vowel raising; p.190 states the alternation cannot be attributed to syllable structure, 'metrical facts' or duration.

sources.citation: Heal, Sarah. 2020. Grammar Sketch of Mashan Miao. SIL e-Books 74. Dallas: SIL International. viii+75 pp. (recovered via Internet Archive copy of sil.org reapdata PDF)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing. RRG syntax sketch (speaker LY = Central hmm, WZ = Southern hma). Sec.1.2 p.6-7: 'The tonal system of Mashan Miao is one of the most complex (Mortensen 2013)'; sec.1.4 p.8 many words monosyllabic; fn.1 p.17 'Tones in Mashan Miao are marked orthographically by the final letter of each word'; Appendix C pp.71-72 gives Southern-vernacular consonant/vowel/tone tables only (9 tones). The word 'stress' never occurs.

sources.note: Bare inventory for Zongdi (Jiaodi zhai): 46 initials, 32 finals, 8 tone values; nothing on stress.

sources.note: p.596 lists 'Central Mashan Hmong'; 'Hmong-Mien is usually described as being exclusively tonal.. we did not have access to sources that would allow us to elaborate on this point.' No data.
